Assumption: the question text is cut off. I have taken 60 to mean 60 % completion, and the quantity asked for to be the mass of X in grams, reported as a multiple of $10^{-2}$ g.
Key concept: phenol heated with Zn dust is reduced to benzene, so X is benzene: $\mathrm{C_6H_5OH + Zn \xrightarrow{\Delta} C_6H_6 + ZnO}$.
The mole ratio of phenol to benzene is $1:1$.
Molar mass of phenol: $6(12)+6(1)+16 = 94\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
Moles of phenol: $n = \dfrac{4.7\ \mathrm{g}}{94\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}} = 0.05\ \mathrm{mol}$.
At 60 % completion, moles of benzene formed: $0.05 \times 0.60 = 0.03\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Molar mass of benzene: $6(12)+6(1) = 78\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
Mass of benzene formed: $0.03\ \mathrm{mol} \times 78\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}} = 2.34\ \mathrm{g} = 234\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{g}$.
Answer: 234

Concept: When phenol is heated with zinc dust, the –OH group is removed and benzene is formed. So X is benzene.
$\mathrm{C_6H_5OH + Zn \xrightarrow{\Delta} C_6H_6 + ZnO}$
Assumption: the truncated text asks for the mass of X formed at 60% completion (standard JEE Main 2023 form of this question).
Step 1: From the equation, 1 mol of phenol gives 1 mol of benzene.
Step 2: $M(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH}) = 6(12)+6(1)+16 = 94\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ and $M(\mathrm{C_6H_6}) = 6(12)+6(1) = 78\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Step 3: Moles of phenol taken: $n = \dfrac{4.7\ \mathrm{g}}{94\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}} = 0.05\ \mathrm{mol}$
Step 4: Moles of benzene formed at 60% completion: $0.60 \times 0.05 = 0.03\ \mathrm{mol}$
Step 5: Mass of benzene formed: $0.03\ \mathrm{mol} \times 78\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}} = 2.34\ \mathrm{g} = 234\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{g}$
Answer: 234
